confirmed_runtime_finding.statement: Nested engine entry from a public callback erases the enclosing budget (fail-open enforcement loss, not memory unsafety). Reproduced with public API only.
confirmed_runtime_finding.evidence_runtime: Harness cases [None, Unlimited, ExplicitBudget, ParseError] -> enforced=[true,false,false,true]; both successful nested cases return Ok([[7]]) with cancel=true, callback_calls=1, same installing thread; the None and ParseError controls return Err("query budget exceeded (cancelled)") proving a real post-callback poll exists and that the loss is caused by the nested install/drop pair, not by absent polling. --require-restoration exits 101.
confirmed_runtime_finding.evidence_source: exec.rs:217-229 install() unconditionally overwrites ACTIVE and sets EXCEEDED=None; exec.rs:198-203 Drop unconditionally sets ACTIVE=OFF, EXCEEDED=None. There is no saved previous state anywhere in the module, so the inner Guard's drop is indistinguishable from returning to idle. Public reachability: lib.rs:1017/1013 query()/query_with_budget() reach lib.rs:1036 install() from inside a FunctionRegistry callback executing under the outer install at the same site.
confirmed_runtime_finding.secondary_defect_confirmed_by_same_root_: set_width/restore_width bracketing (exec.rs:243-266) is also broken across a nested call today: after the child drops ACTIVE to OFF, restore_width is a no-op because it is gated on a.on. Correct save/restore of the whole Limits repairs this as a consequence; no separate fix needed.

minimal_design.accepted_shape: (1) budget::Guard stores a Copy of the previous Limits and the previous EXCEEDED value taken at install time and restores both in Drop; entry from idle saves OFF/None, so no special case is needed. (2) Guard and install become private to `mod budget`; the only crate-visible entry becomes `pub(crate) fn with_budget<T>(b: &QueryBudget, f: impl FnOnce() -> T) -> T`, which constructs the guard internally and returns f's value. (3) The 14 production installers and any direct tests migrate to with_budget. (4) Limits/snapshot/parallel_json_fanout/hit/why are narrowed from pub(crate) to pub(in crate::exec) with a written scope invariant.
minimal_design.why_this_is_the_smallest_sound_boundary: Restoration of a raw CancelPtr is only sound if the restored pointer's owner is still live at restore time. Under a closure-scoped installer that is guaranteed by construction: the parent's `&QueryBudget` borrow is held by a stack frame that strictly encloses the child's dynamic extent, so LIFO is enforced by the call stack rather than asserted. No heap stack of saved states, no Arc cloning into TLS, no owned cancellation handle, no public API change, and no ownership redesign is required to reach that invariant.
minimal_design.cost: Guard grows by one Copy Limits (~6-7 scalar fields) plus one Option<&'static str>; two extra TLS reads at install and two writes at drop. No allocation on any path.

blocking_findings.finding: A saved-Limits patch shipped WITHOUT sealing the installer is not lifetime-sound at the type level. Guard<'a> borrows only the child budget (exec.rs:195 PhantomData<&'a QueryBudget>) and install is pub(crate) and returns the guard by value, so crate-internal safe code can drop guards non-LIFO and drop the parent budget before the child guard restores its pointer.
blocking_findings.evidence: exec.rs:194-234; author's non-executed source/type counterexample (g1=install(&outer); g2=install(&inner); drop(g1); drop(outer); drop(g2); check(0)) type-checks under NLL because g1's borrow of `outer` ends at drop(g1). Current code is immune only because Drop always writes OFF.
blocking_findings.reachability: NOT externally reachable today: lib.rs:26 keeps `mod exec` private, so no external caller can name Guard, install, or Limits; all 14 inspected installers are synchronous, keep the guard in a `_guard` local, return owned concrete types, and never hand a guard to a callback.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Introduce restoration and the sealed with_budget seam in the SAME change. Do not land a two-field restoration patch against the existing returning-Guard interface, and do not compile a test-only pub install that reintroduces non-LIFO.

blocking_findings.finding: Restoration must be Drop-based inside with_budget, not a tail call after f(). Several migrated sites propagate errors mid-body and can unwind under the scope.
blocking_findings.evidence: construct.rs:61 `eval_select(...)?` inside the installed region; construct.rs:97; explain.rs:98; update.rs:729-730 (parse under the budget); lib.rs:1044/1114/1139/1196 `?` inside the match; user callbacks execute arbitrary code and may panic.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: with_budget holds a private RAII restorer; f may return, return Err, or unwind and the parent state is restored identically. A caught unwind that crossed a child scope must therefore see the parent state already restored. panic=abort has no continuation guarantee and needs no handling beyond a comment.

blocking_findings.finding: The existing SAFETY justification becomes false once restoration lands and must be rewritten, because it is the load-bearing argument for two unsafe derefs and two unsafe Send/Sync impls.
blocking_findings.evidence: exec.rs:75-90 ("The Guard lifetime keeps that budget ... alive until the pointer has been cleared"), exec.rs:165-169 and exec.rs:421-431 (`unsafe { cancel.0.as_ref() }`). After the fix, a child guard's drop reinstalls a pointer owned by a DIFFERENT budget than the one its own lifetime parameter borrows, so the current wording no longer covers the stored value.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: State the new invariant explicitly on the module and on CancelPtr: ACTIVE holds either OFF or the Limits of the innermost live with_budget frame on this thread; every stored cancel pointer is owned by a `&QueryBudget` borrow held by a with_budget frame currently on this thread's stack; this holds because install/Guard are unreachable outside `mod budget`, so scopes are strictly nested by the call stack. Also record that only the innermost frame ever writes ACTIVE.

blocking_findings.finding: Restoration must copy the saved Limits value and the saved EXCEEDED value verbatim; reconstructing from the parent's public QueryBudget fields is insufficient.
blocking_findings.evidence: byte_width (exec.rs:243-253) and extra_bytes (exec.rs:273-289) are mutated during execution and are not derivable from QueryBudget; EXCEEDED is sticky for max-rows/max-bytes (exec.rs:409-414) and is currently cleared by both install and drop (exec.rs:201, 229). A handled child error must remain child-local and must not erase a prior parent reason.
blocking_findings.required_resolution: Save `ACTIVE.get()` and `EXCEEDED.get()` before writing the child state; restore both unconditionally in Drop. Keep EXCEEDED=None on child entry (child isolation). Note that deadline and cancel are re-derived from wall clock / live flag on the parent's next poll, so no elapsed time or flag flip during the child is masked.

snapshot_boundary_assessment.verified_from_supplied_source: All four Limits consumers are inside exec.rs and are synchronous, join-before-return, and never install budget state into worker TLS: (a) 2553 parallel_json_fanout() -> par_chunks(...).map(...).collect::<Vec<(usize,String)>>() at 2559-2586 with the on-thread gate at 2591; (b) 2755 snapshot() -> par_chunks(...).collect::<Vec<String>>() at 2758-2780; (c) 8819 EngineSnapshot(snapshot()) captured by reference in fold/reduce, joined at 8829-8832, on-thread gate at 8833; (d) 9784 snapshot() -> par_iter().map(...).collect::<Result<Vec<bool>,String>>()? at 9794-9812 (rayon joins before the collect returns, including on short-circuit). The contrast at 9803-9809 is decisive: functions/view/spatial/local_services/query_now DO worker_install into worker TLS, budget deliberately does NOT. Restoration therefore does not interact with worker state: a nested with_budget executed on a rayon worker writes and restores only that worker's TLS and cannot corrupt the parent thread's ACTIVE.
snapshot_boundary_assessment.ruling: Accept the four audited synchronous consumers as the trusted boundary; this is sufficient and no ownership redesign is warranted. Required tightening (cheap, mechanical, zero call-site churn since all consumers are in exec.rs): narrow Limits, snapshot, parallel_json_fanout, hit and why from pub(crate) to pub(in crate::exec), keeping the existing cfg_attr(not(feature="parallel"), allow(dead_code)) attributes so non-parallel/wasm builds stay warning-clean. Add a doc invariant on snapshot/parallel_json_fanout: the returned Limits is a lifetime-free Copy that must not outlive the with_budget frame it was taken from, and may be used only by scoped parallel iterators that join before that frame returns; enumerate the four call sites and require any new consumer to re-justify.
snapshot_boundary_assessment.residual_risk_and_why_not_blocking: The lifetime-free Copy signature is not a type-level proof against a future internal caller retaining or detaching a snapshot. That hazard is PRE-EXISTING and is not made worse by restoration: today a stale snapshot held past guard drop already carries a dangling pointer even though ACTIVE is set to OFF. Narrowing visibility plus the written invariant is a proportionate response; a lifetime-scoped `with_snapshot(|&Limits| ...)` or a scope token threaded through sjoin::BudgetSnapshot is an acceptable optional hardening, not a condition of this approval. Do not advertise the raw snapshot interface as intrinsically sound for arbitrary internal use.
snapshot_boundary_assessment.unverified: The parallel paths were not exercised at runtime (RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 in the reproduction environment); this assessment is source-level plus the frozen excerpts only.

implementation_requirements: Migrate exactly the 14 sites with byte-equivalent scope coverage. Each migrated site must cover the SAME work as today: construct.rs:60 covers eval_select + instantiate; construct.rs:96 covers eval_select + cbd; construct.rs:123 covers the whole match including both arms; update.rs:728 covers parse_update (parse errors currently occur inside the scope) + apply; explain.rs:93 keeps trace::install() nested INSIDE the budget scope and trace::take() inside it too, preserving the current _tguard-before-_bguard drop order; explain_json.rs:222 likewise; lib.rs sites keep _view_scope created outside/before the budget scope so the budget restore still happens before view_scope drop. A silently widened or narrowed region is a behavior change in byte accounting and deadline coverage.
with_budget must be generic over the return type and must not require the closure to be Send/'static; the migrated bodies capture &mut Graph (update.rs:722-731) and &mut sink (lib.rs:1183-1194).
Keep the child-side !Send marker semantics; a scoped closure makes thread affinity structural, but retain the marker so the guard type cannot be moved if it is ever exposed again.

Verify (grep the whole workspace, including tests, benches, examples, sparq-server, wasm bindings and feature-gated modules) that no install call site remains outside `mod budget` and that the 14-site inventory is complete; the count is currently an author assertion, not something I could verify from excerpts.

Audit the service/service-local byte_savepoint/restore_bytes pair (exec.rs:361-395), which is not in the supplied excerpts: confirm no savepoint/restore pair can straddle a with_budget boundary; if one can, it must be documented or bracketed, since restore_bytes writes ACTIVE.extra_bytes and EXCEEDED directly.

Documentation: state in the public docs of the *_with_budget entry points (or QueryBudget) that a nested engine call made from a user callback is bounded by its own budget only, that the outer budget resumes on return, and that the outer deadline/cancellation is observed at the next poll rather than interrupting callback work. No composite/global budget is being introduced.
Build/check matrix: default, parallel, no-parallel, wasm32 (the deadline field is cfg'd out of Limits, so the saved copy must compile there), service, service-local, params, vectorized, cs-planner.
test_requirements: Regression gate: the exact supplied public harness with --require-restoration must exit 0 after the fix, built against a freshly built engine (not the cached rlib). Keep all four cases including the two controls; the controls are what prove the post-callback poll.

Sealed-seam unit tests: inner tighter than outer and inner looser than outer; outer sticky max-rows/max-bytes set before the nested call and still observed after; child max-rows error not visible to the parent; byte_width/extra_bytes exactly restored (set_width + add_bytes bracketing a nested call, asserted via an exact accounting assertion, not a bound); three-level nesting; nested call returning Ok, returning Err, and panicking through catch_unwind; idle->child->idle returns to OFF/None.

Cancellation identity: outer and inner must use DISTINCT Arc<AtomicBool>; flip the outer flag during the inner scope and assert the parent errors on its next check after restore. Deadline: use an already-past Instant, never sleeps.

Thread/worker coverage with RAYON_NUM_THREADS>1: exercise at least one of the four snapshot paths (e.g. the parallel hash-join at 8814-8834 and the parallel serializer at 2751-2800) with a nested query in a callback, asserting the parent thread's budget is intact afterwards and that no worker-thread state leaks.

Mutation controls that must FAIL if the corresponding piece of restoration is removed: drop the saved Limits -> public harness fails; drop the saved EXCEEDED -> sticky test fails; drop byte_width/extra_bytes from the restore -> exact accounting test fails.

Sealing evidence: a compile_fail doc-test or trybuild case showing that another module cannot name budget::Guard or call budget::install (and therefore cannot forget or early-drop a guard). Do NOT compile or execute the non-LIFO dangling-restore sequence; it is undefined behavior and must remain a source/type argument only.
explicitly_not_required: An Arc/TLS ownership redesign, an owned cancellation handle in TLS, or a heap stack of saved budget states. No concrete need is demonstrated once installation is closure-scoped.
Making the nested call inherit or compose with the outer budget, or making arbitrary callback work interruptible. Out of scope; document instead.
Any public API addition; with_budget stays pub(crate) and exec stays private (lib.rs:26).
source_context_limits: Only excerpts were supplied: exec.rs 68-234, 235-465, 2170-2195, 2530-2610, 2730-2800, 8790-8860, 9765-9830; lib.rs 20-30, 1010-1248; cache.rs 345-382; construct.rs 35-160; explain.rs 75-140; explain_json.rs 195-255; update.rs 510-575, 700-815. I saw code for all 14 claimed install sites but cannot confirm the inventory is exhaustive across the workspace (tests, benches, sparq-server, wasm bindings, feature-gated modules were not shown).

Not supplied and therefore unassessed: the callback dispatch site in functions.rs, the service streaming byte_savepoint/restore_bytes callers, sjoin.rs, cap_alloc consumers, and the existing test suite.

Reproduction was compiled against cached rlibs from commit ed66ef09 with an asserted byte-identical tree at d41ec9f rather than a fresh production build at the merged commit; RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1 means no parallel/snapshot path was executed; no wasm32, service, Miri or full-feature evidence exists.
Deadline, sticky-reason, byte-accounting and unwind behavior are argued from source, not measured; they are covered by the test requirements above.
approval_scope: Design approval only, and conditional on B1-B4 plus the snapshot visibility narrowing being satisfied in the implementation. The implemented diff, the migrated 14 sites' scope equivalence, the rewritten SAFETY invariant text, and real test output (including the mutation controls and a >1-thread run) still require review before protected CI/merge.
